subject: ventures/freelance-retainer-calculator
auditor: agent session (Claude), round 78, see run record
professional: an experienced independent consultant / agency operations lead who prices monthly retainers, writes their overage, rollover and payment clauses, and manages the agency's receivables

evidence.correctness: Ran the engine (scratch script importing app.js) and recomputed by hand. Defaults ($6,000 take-home, $1,800 costs, 160 h, 65%, 20 h, 15%): capacity 160*0.65=104; floor 7800/104=75; retainer 75*20*1.15=1725 = engine 104/75/1725/7800. Usage table: 1725/10=172.50, /15=115, /20=86.25, /25=69, with 5 h overage at floor (1725+375)/25=84 = engine and retainer-vs-hourly.html. Income-goal at 60% fill: 0.6*84=50.4 h*75=3780+1725=5505, short 2295, required fill 6075/(84*75)=96.43%, 30.6 h, retainer to close 4020 = engine and will-this-retainer page. Rollover: break-even 1725/75=23, buffer 3; unlimited 30 h -> 57.50/hr, cap 23 h -> 75, expire 86.25 = engine. vs-pricing page: 6000/104*20=1153.85, diff 571.15, x12 6853.80 = page. Arithmetic is right. But the cash-float output is the wrong quantity: calculateCashFloat(plan.target, ...) multiplies the whole-month revenue target ($7,800, all clients) by days/30, so a $1,725/month client on month-end Net 30 is shown as making you 'float $15,600'. Standard receivables arithmetic (outstanding AR = billings per day x days to cash; e.g. DSO definition in any managerial-accounting text) gives this client's exposure as 1725*60/30 = $3,450, or at most its delivery cost. The headline 'Cash you lend the client' is overstated 4.5x on defaults, and the proposal summary carries the same figure. Held at 2.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked end to end via the engine and node tests: hourly floor and retainer, 10-30 h package table, 50/75/100/125% usage table, offered-price check, income-goal coverage with fill rate, rollover comparison (three clauses), payment-terms float, copy/download summary, share link encode/decode, local draft, opt-out persistence -- all present; 28 node tests green. served-copy: no placeholder or retired origin. Unrecorded: README event list omits client_offer_compared (app.js:789). No stubs/TODOs.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in subject root: tests 28, pass 28, fail 0 (app.test.mjs and page.test.mjs use top-level asserts, so 28 tests hold many more assertions). Six seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: floor from income only, arrears15 days 45->40, rollover cap min->max, hoursAtFloor divisor, expected fill on full capacity all CAUGHT; coversFloor >= -> > at app.js:425 SURVIVED (no exact-floor boundary case in usage rows). Strong suite, but it pins the wrong float design ($15,600 asserted at app.test.mjs:97, page.test.mjs:27), so it would block the fix rather than catch the bug.
evidence.craft: Read app.js (920 lines), share.mjs, index.html and the eight content pages. Pure exported functions, input validation with clear messages, try/catch around storage, DOM code guarded for node import. Defects: formatRolloverAdvice embeds the engine's recommendation string, which formats money without a currency symbol ('30 hours for 1725 -- 57.5/hr, below the 75/hr floor', app.js:518), so the downloaded proposal mixes '$75/hr' and '75/hr'; the summary prints internal planning text in a document labelled a client proposal; event list drift. Acceptable to a code reviewer with notes.
evidence.claims: vs-bonsai.html claims about the competitor: paid subscription platform (backed: third-party pricing reviews and Capterra list paid Basic/Essentials/Premium/Elite plans, trial not free plan; hellobonsai.com itself unreachable from this session, DNS blocked); proposals/contracts/invoicing/time tracking (backed by the same reviews); 'its templates include a retainer agreement' (backed: hellobonsai.com/contract-template/monthly-retainer-agreement and consulting-retainer appear in search); 'publishes a general hourly-rate explorer by skill and role' (backed: hellobonsai.com/freelance-rates, Product Hunt 'Bonsai Freelance Rate Explorer'). Page asserts no Bonsai price (test enforces) and disclaims affiliation; cites only the homepage with no retrieval date (low). Unbacked or wrong own claims: retainer-payment-terms.html:61 '$15,600 ... working capital you are lending the client' (wrong base, see correctness); unused-hour-rollover.html:21 headline 'unpaid work next month' and 'Gift $750' (line 68) contradicted by the engine's own two-month figure (40 h for $3,450 = $86.25/hr, exactly the paid rate); will-this-retainer page:22 'Every "what should I charge" calculator divides ...' unbacked generalisation; how-many-retainer-hours.html:52 'up to 30 hours ... still keep at least half the month' when 52 h would (30 is only the largest listed option). Disclaimer present on every page and README.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: priced the default 20 h retainer, read the usage, rollover and payment-terms views, downloaded the proposal. The price and the usage break-even are usable. The 'client-ready' proposal (index.html:22, Download proposal) cannot be sent as is: it tells the client the freelancer's take-home goal ($6,000) and costs, says 'You need to float $15,600 ... from savings', and gives a 'Walk-away' line and the floor at which unpaid extras hurt -- the consultant's negotiating position. A practitioner must hand-edit it every time.
evidence.domain: Compared with retainer practice: (1) Overage priced at the floor ($75) below the in-retainer effective rate ($86.25); Bonsai's own consulting retainer template sample prices 20 h at $5,500 ($275/h) with overage at $325 -- overage at or above the effective rate is the norm. Here a client buying a 10 h block plus 10 h overage pays 862.50+750=1612.50 < 1725 for the same 20 hours, rewarding under-buying. (2) Cash float based on the whole-month target rather than this client's billings (receivables/DSO arithmetic). (3) Rollover framed as unpaid work; across the two months unlimited one-month rollover delivers exactly the hours paid for (twoMonthEffective 86.25); the real risks a practitioner names are capacity spikes and accumulating deferred-delivery liability, and the recommended clause (cap + expiry) is sound. Capacity-share (>50% one client) guidance and margin-on-floor buffer are reasonable.

The 'client-ready' copy/download proposal prints the freelancer's take-home goal and costs, 'You need to float $X from savings', the walk-away line and the break-even at which unpaid extras hurt -- internal negotiating data in a client document

Overage ('Additional work') is priced at the floor ($75), below the retainer's own effective rate ($86.25): a 10 h block plus 10 h overage costs the client $1,612.50 vs $1,725 for the 20 h block, rewarding under-buying; practice (e.g. Bonsai's consulting retainer template, $275/h effective, $325 overage) bills overage at or above the effective rate

Rollover guidance calls rolled hours 'unpaid work' and a '$750 gift'; the engine's own two-month view shows unlimited one-month rollover delivers 40 h for $3,450 = $86.25/h, exactly the paid rate. The real risk (capacity spike, accumulating deferred delivery) is not what the page says

verdict: The pricing arithmetic is right: floor, retainer, package table, usage table, income-goal coverage, rollover figures and the vs-pricing comparison all recompute by hand to the cent, and the test suite caught 5 of 6 seeded mutants. The vs-Bonsai competitor claims (paid platform, proposals/contracts/invoicing/time tracking, retainer template, rate explorer) are backed by secondary sources and assert no price. It misses the bar on correctness and claims: the cash-float figure multiplies the freelancer's whole-month target instead of this client's billings ($15,600 vs $3,450 on defaults) and the payment-terms page sells that as cash lent to the client. A retainer practitioner would also reject overage billed below the retainer's effective rate, the 'unpaid work' framing of rollover that the engine's own two-month figure contradicts, and a 'client-ready' proposal that discloses the freelancer's take-home goal and walk-away.
